title: Eco-friendly pH monitoring in aquaculture: A comparative study of biomass waste extracts with different setup designs
author: Nadi, Najafabadi, et al.

steps.title: Prepare plant extracts
steps.instruction: Rinse fresh mango leaves sequentially with tap water then distilled water, dry at 65 °C for 48 h, grind and sieve to ≤120 µm; dry coffee grounds identically; reflux 100 g of each dried powder in 500 mL distilled water at 100 °C for 30 min, centrifuge at 8000 × g for 15 min; boil 100 g shredded red cabbage leaves in 500 mL distilled water for 30 min and filter; store all extracts at –20 °C.

steps.title: Prepare pH standards and load cuvettes
steps.instruction: Serially dilute 1 M H₃PO₄ and 1 M NaOH to create standard solutions covering pH 1–13, adjusting dilution ratios precisely; pipette 0.5 mL of each plant extract into cuvettes containing 3 mL of the appropriate standard solution or aquaculture pond sample; use a Samsung A12 smartphone for imaging; employ standard spectrophotometer cuvettes (4.5 cm height, 3.5 mL capacity, 190–2500 nm optical range).

steps.title: Assemble photometric chambers
steps.instruction: Construct four imaging chambers: (a) black corrugated polypropylene box, 15 cm wide, 5 cm high, with a 2 cm triangular cutout sample holder; (b) identical white polypropylene box; (c) polyethylene pipe assembly, 22 cm long, 4.5 cm inner diameter, coated internally with 0.5 cm‑thick translucent hot‑melt adhesive, fitted with an Eveready LC1L2A LED source and a lateral sampling port 7 cm from the LED; (d) polystyrene tray using a white foam packaging tray, positioning the smartphone 15 cm above the cuvette and using the phone’s integrated LED flash for illumination.

steps.title: Capture images of samples
steps.instruction: Place each cuvette in the chosen photometric chamber, then acquire a 24‑bit JPEG image with the smartphone (average file size 1.4 MB, resolution 4000 × 1800 px) under the controlled illumination conditions.

steps.title: Process images for chromatic index
steps.instruction: Open the JPEG in Color Grab (v3.4.1) on Android, select three circular regions of interest (ROIs) per image, record the RGB values (0–255) for each ROI, average the values across ROIs, and calculate the normalized chromatic index R/(G + B); repeat the measurement five times and compute the standard deviation.

steps.title: Validate pH with conventional meters
steps.instruction: Measure the pH of each real pond sample using three meters (pH 2700, Eutech; AB15 basic; Fisher Accumet), performing five replicates per sample and calculating the standard deviation for consistency.

steps.title: Test selectivity with interfering substances
steps.instruction: Add ammonia (2 mg L⁻¹), nitrite (0.5 mg L⁻¹), and nitrate (50 mg L⁻¹) to separate aliquots of pond water to simulate maximum permissible concentrations, then proceed with the standard imaging and analysis workflow.

steps.title: Analyze pond water pH with extracts
steps.instruction: Collect water from eight aquaculture ponds, filter each sample through a 0.22 µm nylon syringe filter, mix the filtrate with mango leaf extract, image the mixture using the top‑view tray configuration and the smartphone, and calculate pH values from the calibration curve equation.
